problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y+z=14 \\  & y+z=8 \\  & z=4\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+5y-2z=1 \\  & y+3z=0 \\  & z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form.

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-5){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 18 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x=18 \\  & y=-3 \\  & z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=18$, $y=-3$, and $z=1.$ Or, in vector form $⟨18,-3,1⟩.$
